## Description {#details}

The <code><Link to="/docs/api/namespaces/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/type-traits">type&#95;traits</Link></code> namespace offers a comprehensive suite of type trait templates and metaprogramming utilities employed throughout the µTest++ framework.

This includes templates for function traits, type lists, identity, value wrappers, and compile-time checks for container types, floating point types, and type convertibility. It also provides generic integral and floating point constant wrappers, as well as mechanisms for SFINAE and requirements checking.

These utilities facilitate advanced template programming, type deduction, and compile-time introspection, supporting the flexible and type-safe design of the framework.

All definitions within this namespace are implemented in the <code>include/micro-os-plus</code> folder to maintain a structured and modular codebase.

The <code>has&#95;epsilon&#95;v</code> variable template evaluates to <code>true</code> if the given type <code>T</code> defines a member named <code>epsilon</code>. This trait is determined at compile time using SFINAE and the <code>is&#95;valid</code> utility, and is used throughout the µTest++ framework to enable generic handling of types that represent floating-point values or require precision control.

### is&#95;floating&#95;point&#95;v {#abfe0c2413694bb3a6dcdf1da303c38db}

<MemberDefinition
  template={<>template &lt;class T&gt;</>}
  prototype={<>auto micro&#95;os&#95;plus::micro&#95;test&#95;plus::type&#95;traits::is&#95;floating&#95;point&#95;v = false</>}
  labels = {["constexpr"]}>
Variable template to determine if a type is a floating point type.

---

The <code>is&#95;floating&#95;point&#95;v</code> variable template evaluates to <code>true</code> if the given type <code>T</code> is a floating point type (<code>float</code>, <code>double</code>, or <code>long double</code>). For all other types, it evaluates to <code>false</code>. This trait is used throughout the µTest++ framework to enable type-safe handling and specialisation for floating point types in template metaprogramming.
